results.title: Flemish Land Agency (VLM)
results.description:
​​​​​​​​The Vlaam​se Landmaatschappij is committed to developing resilient open spaces that are brimming with life. We are enhancing our countryside and open spaces to enable them to better endure urbanisation, fragmentation and climate change. We are collaborating on policy and investing in soil and water quality, biodiversity and infrastructure. We are striving for beautiful, healthy urban and rural environments that are a pleasure to live and work in, and where there is plenty of space for relaxation. We do so with uncompromising passion and expertise, and in constant collaboration with our partners. 

Flanders is one of the most densely populated and prosperous regions in Europe. The Vlaamse Landmaatschappij promotes the Flanders countryside and open spaces on many fronts. If we invest intelligently in our countryside and open spaces, they will be better able to protect us against the effects of climate change, such as flooding and droughts. Farmers will be able to produce food, the survival chances of plants and animals will increase, and space will emerge for meeting places and leisure activities.​

results.title: WeForest
results.description: WeForest is an international non-profit organisation implementing Forest and Landscape Restoration (FLR) projects in tropical regions for the benefit of people, nature and climate. Our FLR approach is tailored to each project context and integrates a wide range of interventions within broader livelihood development programmes. These aim to address both the causes and consequences of natural resource degradation and deforestation by incentivising sustainable livelihoods, ensuring Forest Governance & Stewardship, and promoting the conservation, restoration and sustainable management of natural ecosystems. As part of our monitoring, evaluation & learning (MEL) processes, WeForest collects biodiversity data. By sharing this monitoring data through the GBIF platform, WeForest aims at advancing its objectives on open science, for the benefit of research and restoration communities.
